domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: A single application by an employee for a span of leave of one type, moving through an approval lifecycle. GP-008 makes a completed approval immutable: an APPROVED row is never mutated; cancelling it inserts a NEW LeaveRequest row (status CANCELLED) whose reversesRequestId points at the untouched original. Canonical cross-module data contract — 15 fields; must not gain, lose or rename a field without a matching repository/schema change.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestReversal
domain_entities.purpose: Derived domain concept (no table of its own) describing the two-row representation of a cancelled-after-approval leave: the untouched original APPROVED LeaveRequest plus the NEW CANCELLED LeaveRequest whose reversesRequestId points at it. Named home for the cross-row invariants (immutability, uniqueness, release-once).

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
attributes: available: number (computed = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays; never persisted)
domain_entities.purpose: Per-employee, per-leave-type, per-accrual-period reservation ledger. Unchanged in shape by this feature; the release triggered by a reversal must happen exactly once, in the same transaction as the reversal insert, keyed off the ORIGINAL row's requestedDays.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
attributes: action: AuditAction (CANCEL for both cancellation paths)
entityId: string (mutated row in-place; NEW reversal row for a reversal)
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable record of every state-changing operation (GP-002). Exactly one CANCEL entry per cancellation; for a reversal it is anchored on the NEW row (entityId = reversal id, beforeState = original APPROVED, afterState = new CANCELLED) so the untouched original leaves no UPDATE trail.

domain_entities.name: Notification
attributes: relatedEntityId: string | null (the NEW reversal row id)
domain_entities.purpose: Synchronous in-app notice to the requester that their leave was cancelled. Unchanged by this feature; the reversal path sends the same single cancellation notification as the in-place path, addressed to the original request's employeeId.

modules.name: shared-types
owns: requestedDays(startDate, endDate) canonical inclusive day-count helper
NOTE: no new cross-module value type — the reversal is represented by LeaveRequest itself

ILeaveService + LeaveService (cancel branches: in-place for DRAFT/SUBMITTED, insert-new-row reversal for APPROVED)

owns: IBalanceRepository + PgLeaveBalanceRepository (findByKey with forUpdate row lock, update)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Schema + model + repository: reverses_request_id
recommended_phases.rationale: Add the nullable self-referencing column first so every later layer has a real field to carry. New knex migration migrations/<ts>_add_reverses_request_id_to_leave_requests.js (alterTable add reverses_request_id referencing leave_requests.id + partial unique index WHERE reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL; down drops index then column). Then leave.model.ts gains reversesRequestId: string | null (CreateLeaveRequestInput follows via Omit), and leave.repository.ts threads it end-to-end: LeaveRequestRow, COLUMNS, mapRow, the 15-value INSERT, and a new findByReversesRequestId(reversesRequestId, client) for the duplicate-reversal guard. No service or route change yet, so the existing suite stays green.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — LeaveService.cancel: reversal branch for APPROVED
recommended_phases.rationale: The single behavioural change, confined to leave.service.ts. Split cancel on the loaded request's status: DRAFT/SUBMITTED keep the current in-place repository.update(... status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt ...) path untouched; APPROVED instead calls repository.create({ ...original fields, status: CANCELLED, reversesRequestId: request.id, cancelledBy: actor.id, cancelledAt: now }) and never calls update on the original id. Guard a second reversal via findByReversesRequestId -> ConflictError. The balance release (usedDays -= request.requestedDays) stays exactly where it is, inside the same uow.withTransaction, executed once, with the row locked via resolveBalance(..., client, true). The CANCEL audit entry is still written, with entityId = the NEW row id and beforeState = the original APPROVED row. The notification is unchanged. assertCanCancel and the startDate timing guard are unchanged.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Read-model exposure + unit tests
recommended_phases.rationale: reversesRequestId reaches the wire for free once Phase 1 added it to COLUMNS/mapRow, so GET /leaves and GET /leaves/:id need no route edit — this phase verifies and pins it. Extend tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts: (a) cancel APPROVED -> the fake repository records ZERO update calls against the original id, exactly ONE create with status CANCELLED and reversesRequestId === original.id, the original fixture still reads APPROVED, usedDays decremented by exactly requestedDays once, one CANCEL audit entry, one notification, all inside a single withTransaction callback with the stub client forwarded; (b) cancel DRAFT and cancel SUBMITTED still mutate in place and create no new row; (c) the reversal row is returned by list/getById with reversesRequestId populated. Update FakeLeaveRepository to implement findByReversesRequestId and fixtures to carry reversesRequestId: null.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Smoke proof against real Postgres
recommended_phases.rationale: Extend scripts/smoke.js (Postgres mode) with the acceptance proof only a real database can give: create -> submit -> approve a request, then cancel it, then assert via GET /leaves/:id that the ORIGINAL id still reads status === 'APPROVED' with approverId/decidedAt intact, and that a second row exists whose reversesRequestId equals the original id and whose status === 'CANCELLED'. Assert the balance usedDays returned to its pre-approval value exactly once (not twice). This stage catches a repository COLUMNS/mapRow omission that unit fakes cannot see.

architecture_md_update:
## GP-008 — Approved leave is reversed, not mutated

### Summary

A completed approval is immutable (GP-008). Cancelling a DRAFT or SUBMITTED request keeps its current in-place behaviour; cancelling an APPROVED request leaves the approved row byte-identical and inserts a NEW `leave_requests` row with `status = CANCELLED` whose `reversesRequestId` points at the original. The balance release, the CANCEL audit record and the cancellation notification are unchanged in effect and all occur exactly once, inside a single unit of work.

### Domain entities

- **LeaveRequest** — gains one nullable field `reversesRequestId: string | null` (null for every ordinary request; set only on a reversal row). Canonical shape 14 -> 15 fields; `CreateLeaveRequestInput = Omit<LeaveRequest,'id'>` follows automatically. `UpdateLeaveRequestDto` must NOT gain `reversesRequestId` — the link is set at insert and immutable thereafter.
- **LeaveRequestReversal** — derived concept (no table): the two-row representation of a cancelled-after-approval leave. Named home for the cross-row invariants (immutability, uniqueness, release-once).
- **LeaveBalance**, **AuditLog**, **Notification** — unchanged in shape; only their participation in the reversal transaction is specified.

### Lifecycle states (introduced / folded in)

Existing canonical states unchanged: LeaveRequest DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED; LeaveBalance OPEN | CLOSED; LeavePolicy DRAFT | ACTIVE | SUPERSEDED; Employee ACTIVE | TERMINATED | ON_LEAVE; AuditLog RECORDED; Notification PENDING | SENT | READ | ARCHIVED; LeaveType static.

New states:
1. **LeaveRequest.CANCELLED_IN_PLACE** — derived, not stored: `status = CANCELLED AND reversesRequestId = null`. Produced by cancelling a DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; the same row is mutated.
2. **LeaveRequest.CANCELLED_REVERSAL** — derived, not stored: `status = CANCELLED AND reversesRequestId != null`. Produced by cancelling an APPROVED request; a NEW row, the original left APPROVED.
3. **LeaveRequestReversal.CREATED** — the reversal row is inserted and the balance released in one transaction.
4. **LeaveRequestReversal.TERMINAL** — a reversal row is itself immutable and can never be submitted, approved, rejected or cancelled again.

No new stored enum member is added to `LeaveStatus`; the two CANCELLED variants are discriminated by `reversesRequestId`, which is why that field must be on the read model.

### Transition table

- `cancelDraftInPlace`: DRAFT -> CANCELLED (same row; no balance touch; reversesRequestId stays null).
- `cancelSubmittedInPlace`: SUBMITTED -> CANCELLED (same row; pendingDays -= requestedDays; reversesRequestId stays null).
- `cancelApprovedByReversal`: APPROVED -> (original unchanged) + insert CANCELLED reversal row with reversesRequestId = original.id; usedDays -= requestedDays.
- `reversalTerminal`: reversal row -> no further transitions.

### Business rules

- **GP-008 immutability**: once APPROVED, `status`, `approverId`, `approvalComment` and `decidedAt` are immutable. Cancelling an APPROVED request performs NO UPDATE on that row (including `cancelledBy`/`cancelledAt`, which stay null on the original).
- **Reversal representation**: insert a NEW LeaveRequest with `status = CANCELLED`, `cancelledBy = actor.id`, `cancelledAt = now`, `reversesRequestId = original.id`. The reversal row copies `employeeId`, `leaveTypeCode`, `startDate`, `endDate` and `requestedDays` verbatim from the original; `requestedDays` is copied, never re-derived.
- **In-place cancellation preserved** for DRAFT/SUBMITTED (same row mutated; `reversesRequestId` stays null).
- **Balance release exactly once**, in the same transaction: DRAFT releases nothing; SUBMITTED releases full `requestedDays` from `pendingDays`; APPROVED releases full `requestedDays` from `usedDays` (no pro-rating). Keyed off the ORIGINAL row's `requestedDays`.
- **At most one reversal per original**: `reversesRequestId` is unique among non-null values (partial unique index); a second cancel of an already-reversed APPROVED request is rejected with `ConflictError` rather than inserting a second row or releasing twice.
- **Reversal row is terminal**: a row with non-null `reversesRequestId` can never be submitted, approved, rejected or cancelled again. Authorization and the timing guard are evaluated against the ORIGINAL request.
- **Authorization unchanged**: owner may cancel own DRAFT/SUBMITTED; an APPROVED request only by the requester's direct manager (`employee.managerId === actor.id`) or an ADMIN. Timing guard unchanged: blocked once `startDate <= today` (UTC day comparison) with `ConflictError`.
- **Audit + notification**: exactly one CANCEL AuditLog per cancellation; for a reversal `entityId` = NEW reversal row id, `beforeState` = original APPROVED, `afterState` = new CANCELLED. Exactly one cancellation Notification to the original's `employeeId`, `relatedEntityId` = reversal row id.
- **Wire honesty**: the read model exposes `reversesRequestId` so a client can distinguish the untouched original (APPROVED, null) from the reversal (CANCELLED, set).
- **Role-scoped visibility** applies identically to reversal rows (they carry the original's `employeeId`); an unauthorized single-read returns the same 404 as a nonexistent id.

### Conceptual tables

- **leave_requests** — fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date, end_date, requested_days, reason, status, approver_id, approval_comment, submitted_at, decided_at, cancelled_by, cancelled_at, reverses_request_id. PK id. FKs: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code; approver_id -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id; reverses_request_id -> leave_requests.id. Indexes: `reverses_request_id` partial UNIQUE (non-null only) — enforces at-most-one reversal per original (the exactly-once release guarantee) and serves reversal lookup; `employee_id` for role-scoped filters; `status` for status filters/lifecycle lookups; `(leave_type_code, start_date)` for type+range queries and ORDER BY start_date DESC; `(employee_id, status)` retained; `approver_id` and `cancelled_by` for FK support.
- **leave_balances** — fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days. PK id. FKs: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code. Index: unique `(employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end)` — findByKey resolves exactly one row per accrual period; `employee_id` for per-employee reads.
- **audit_logs** — fields: id, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, before_state, after_state, occurred_at. PK id. FK: actor_id -> employees.id. Indexes: `(entity_type, entity_id)`; `actor_id`.
- **notifications** — fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at. PK id. FK: recipient_id -> employees.id. Indexes: `(recipient_id, status)`; `(related_entity_type, related_entity_id)`.

One schema change only: `leave_requests` gains nullable `reverses_request_id` (self-FK) plus a partial unique index, delivered as a new knex migration following the existing add-column pattern. Immutability is enforced by the write path, not the schema.

### Repositories (interfaces + concrete implementations)

- **ILeaveRepository / PgLeaveRequestRepository** — `create(input, client?)`, `findById(id, client?)`, `update(id, changes, client?)`, `findByQuery(params, client?)`, `findByReversesRequestId(reversesRequestId, client?)`. Backed by PostgreSQL via the shared pg Pool; optional trailing `PoolClient` joins a caller-owned transaction.
- **IBalanceRepository / PgLeaveBalanceRepository** — `create`, `findById`, `findByKey(employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, client?, forUpdate?)`, `update`. `findByKey` takes `forUpdate` to SELECT ... FOR UPDATE before a release write.
- **IAuditRepository / PgAuditLogRepository** — `create(input, client?)`, `findById(id, client?)`.
- **INotificationRepository / PgNotificationRepository** — `create(input, client?)`, `findById(id, client?)`, `updateStatus(id, status, readAt, client?)`.

### Module boundaries

Presentation (`leave.routes.ts`, Fastify handlers, `resolveActor`, `parseCreateBody`, `parseQuery`, `sendError`) -> Application (`ILeaveService`/`LeaveService` plus composed sibling services) -> Domain (models + pure rules, no I/O) -> Infrastructure (repositories, `IUnitOfWork`/`PgUnitOfWork`, pg Pool, migrations). The change is confined to the **leave** module plus one migration; no new module and no new cross-module value type. `reversesRequestId` is a field on an entity owned by exactly one module, so it lives in `src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts`, not shared types.

### Dependency map

Edges: `leave -> {balance, audit, notification, employee, policy, validation, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-date, shared-auth}`; `balance -> {employee, policy, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-date}`; `policy -> {leave-type, shared-types, shared-errors}`; `leave-type -> {shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db}`; `employee -> {shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-auth}`; `audit -> {shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db}`; `notification -> {shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db}`; `validation -> {shared-types, shared-errors}`; `shared-date -> {shared-errors}`; `shared-auth -> {shared-types, shared-errors}`; `shared-db -> {shared-errors}`.

Topological order: shared-errors -> shared-types -> shared-db -> shared-date -> shared-auth -> leave-type -> policy -> employee -> audit -> notification -> validation -> balance -> leave. Every edge points from a later module to an earlier one; no cycle. `leave` remains the sole orchestrator. All cross-module imports go through each module's `index.ts`.

### Cross-cutting contracts

- **Auth**: `request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole }`, `EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'`. Identity/role from a JWT bearer verified by `registerAuth` in `src/shared/auth/` (populates `request.user` from `payload.sub`/`payload.role`). RBAC enforced at the route boundary by `resolveActor` and in the service by `assertCanCancel` — never inline in a handler. All leave endpoints require a valid token; `POST /auth/login` is the only public path.
- **Transaction**: cancellation is one unit of work. Every repository/service method that must join a caller's transaction takes an optional trailing `client?: PoolClient` defaulting to the shared pool. `LeaveService.cancel` acquires a client via `IUnitOfWork.withTransaction` (PgUnitOfWork: pool.connect, BEGIN, run callback, COMMIT, ROLLBACK on throw, always release) and passes it to `repository.create` (reversal row), `balanceRepository.findByKey(..., client, forUpdate = true)`, `balanceRepository.update`, `auditService.record` and `notificationService.create`. No repository ever issues BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. The DRAFT/SUBMITTED in-place path uses the same single transaction. Read paths open no transaction.
- **Error/response**: errors return `{ error: string; code: string }`. Validation -> 400 (ValidationError, 'VALIDATION'); authentication -> 401 (UnauthorizedError, 'UNAUTHORIZED'); authorization -> 403 (ForbiddenError, 'FORBIDDEN'); not found -> 404 (NotFoundError, 'NOT_FOUND'); invalid state transition or a second reversal -> 409 (ConflictError, 'CONFLICT'); any other throw -> 500 `{ error: 'Internal Server Error' }`. `GET /leaves/:id` returns the same 404 for an invisible request as for a nonexistent one. `POST /leaves/:id/cancel` returns 200 with the resulting row: the mutated original for DRAFT/SUBMITTED, or the NEW CANCELLED reversal row (carrying `reversesRequestId`) for APPROVED.

### Golden-principle compliance

GP-001 (repositories, no inline SQL in the service); GP-002 (CANCEL audit still written for both branches); GP-003 (validation at the API boundary and in ValidationService); GP-005 (RBAC at the route boundary and in `assertCanCancel`); GP-006 (handlers funnel through `sendError`).

### Recommended phases

1. **Schema + model + repository: reverses_request_id** — migration (add nullable self-FK column + partial unique index), `leave.model.ts` gains `reversesRequestId`, `leave.repository.ts` threads it through `LeaveRequestRow`/`COLUMNS`/`mapRow`/INSERT and adds `findByReversesRequestId`. (~3 files)
2. **LeaveService.cancel: reversal branch for APPROVED** — split `cancel` on status; APPROVED inserts a new row and never updates the original; balance release unchanged and once; audit anchored on the new row; second reversal -> ConflictError. (~1 file)
3. **Read-model exposure + unit tests** — verify `reversesRequestId` reaches the wire; unit tests for the reversal branch, the preserved in-place paths, and list/getById exposure. (~2 files)
4. **Smoke proof against real Postgres** — extend `scripts/smoke.js`: create -> submit -> approve -> cancel, assert the original still reads APPROVED with `approverId`/`decidedAt` intact, a second row references it with status CANCELLED, and `usedDays` returned exactly once. (~1 file)

### Open questions

1. Should reversal rows appear in the default `GET /leaves` result set, or be excluded/hidden behind an explicit flag?
2. Should the reversal row copy `approverId`/`approvalComment`/`decidedAt` from the original, or leave them null?
3. Does the untouched original APPROVED row still occupy its date range for overlap/duplicate-leave detection after it has been reversed?

### Consistency flags

- The web client's `getAvailableLeaveActions(status, role, isOwner)` currently treats `status === CANCELLED` as terminal and `APPROVED` as non-cancellable for the owner. After this change an APPROVED request IS cancellable by a manager/ADMIN, and the original row keeps reading APPROVED after reversal — the client must key off `reversesRequestId`, not status alone.
- `docs/DOMAIN.md` remains stale/non-canonical; this slice extends `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and does not contradict it.
- Pre-existing unresolved items (no controller layer; `LeavePolicyStatus` module-local; `notifications.status` default `'unread'` outside `NotificationStatus`; `approvalComment`/`submittedAt` never populated) are untouched and remain open.

business_rules:
Consolidated decision. Questions 1 and 9 are the same question, 2 is a subset of 7, and 4 overlaps 7 — answered once each below, so treat them as ONE decision rather than three.

GUIDING PRINCIPLE, apply it to anything not covered here: the APPROVED row is immutable in STORAGE — no column on it changes after approval. Anything a client needs about the reversal lives either on the reversal row or is DERIVED at read time. And any quantity has exactly one source of truth.

1 + 9. GET /leaves DEFAULT: return BOTH rows unfiltered, plus an optional query filter so a client can ask for only originals or only reversals. Do not hide rows by default — a wire contract that silently omits state is how a client comes to believe an approved request is still live. Document explicitly that an unfiltered count double-counts a reversed request, and that status=CANCELLED returns BOTH in-place cancellations and reversal rows.

2 + 7. WHAT THE REVERSAL ROW CARRIES: copy employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date and end_date verbatim (see 4). Set approverId, approvalComment, decidedAt and submittedAt to NULL — the reversal was never itself approved, and copying approval data onto it blurs exactly the boundary GP-008 draws. Provenance is reachable by following reversesRequestId, and a client that wants 'approved by X, then cancelled by Y' in one view resolves it at read time rather than by duplicating approval fields onto a row that was never approved.

3. DATE OCCUPANCY — take option 1: a reversed original NO LONGER occupies its dates. Any overlap or 'already on leave' check must exclude APPROVED rows that have a reversal pointing at them. The reasoning is that the balance was released, so the employee has those days back; leaving the dates occupied would refund the days and simultaneously forbid re-booking them, which is incoherent from the employee's point of view. Do NOT defer this: no overlap check exists today, which is precisely why the rule is cheap to state now and expensive to retrofit once one is written against the wrong assumption. Record it in ARCHITECTURE.md as a binding rule even though nothing consumes it yet.

4. Copy employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date and end_date VERBATIM — a self-describing row. Your impact note is decisive on its own: a null employee_id makes the reversal invisible to the requester and their manager under role-scoped visibility, and a null start_date silently drops it from ORDER BY start_date DESC and every date-range filter. A tombstone nobody can see is not a tombstone.

5. RELEASED QUANTITY — take option 3: store requested_days = 0 on the reversal row, and always read the released quantity from the ORIGINAL via reverses_request_id. One source of truth for the amount (the original), and a zero that makes double-counting structurally impossible rather than relying on every future aggregate to remember a filter. This is consistent with 7: the row describes WHICH leave was reversed via its dates, while carrying no day count of its own. Do not re-derive with requestedDays(startDate, endDate) — a re-derivation that ever disagrees with the original is the BR-001 two-sources-of-truth anti-pattern you correctly name.

6. EXACTLY-ONCE — take option 3: a partial UNIQUE index on reverses_request_id WHERE reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL, PLUS a service-level guard, with the repository mapping the unique-violation (23505) to ConflictError. The index is what makes a concurrent double-cancellation impossible rather than unlikely; the service guard is what gives the caller a clean 409 instead of a surfaced constraint error. Both, not either.

8. SECOND REVERSAL — reject with ConflictError(409) when findByReversesRequestId(original.id) already returns a row. Not idempotent-200: the two calls are not the same request, and returning 200 would tell a client its cancellation succeeded when an earlier, different actor's cancellation is what actually stands — the audit trail and the 'who cancelled this' answer would then disagree with the response. This makes findByReversesRequestId load-bearing, which is the intent.

AUDIT: use a distinct AuditAction.REVERSE for the reversal (not CANCEL), and write TWO audit records in the same transaction — one whose entityId is the original (beforeState = the APPROVED row, afterState = the new CANCELLED row) and one whose entityId is the new row (beforeState = null, afterState = the new row). Either single record leaves one of the two rows unaudited, and the audit log is the only record of who reversed what. [BINDING RULE — operator decision resolving: Should reversal rows (status CANCELLED, reversesRequestId set) appear in the default GET /leaves result set, or be excluded/hidden behind an explicit flag?; Should the reversal row copy approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt from the original APPROVED request, or leave them null?; Does the untouched original APPROVED row still occupy its date range for overlap/duplicate-leave detection after it has been reversed?; What does the reversal row carry in start_date / end_date / leave_type_code / employee_id — copies of the original, or nulls?; Is the reversal row's requested_days copied verbatim from the original, or re-derived via the shared requestedDays(startDate, endDate) helper?; Is reverses_request_id constrained to at most one non-null row per original (partial unique index), or is it a plain non-unique index?; What field values does the NEW CANCELLED reversal row carry for the fields it does not own — specifically requestedDays, startDate/endDate/leaveTypeCode, and approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt?; May an APPROVED request be reversed more than once — i.e. is a second cancel of the same original id rejected, and how?; Should GET /leaves return reversal rows by default, or only when explicitly asked for?; apply everywhere these apply, not in one place only]
auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity and role are obtained from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing `registerAuth` preHandler in `src/shared/auth/index.ts`, which populates `request.user` from `payload.sub` (id) and `payload.role`; the canonical `AuthUser` type lives in `src/shared/auth/`. RBAC is enforced at the API boundary by the route-level `resolveActor` helper (throws UnauthorizedError on a missing/invalid actor) and in the service by `assertCanCancel` — never inline in a handler. Cancel authorization is unchanged by this feature: the owner may cancel their own DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; only an APPROVED request may be cancelled by a non-owner, and then only by the requester's direct manager (`employee.managerId === actor.id`) or an ADMIN (exempt from the direct-manager check). All leave endpoints require a valid token; `POST /auth/login` is the only public path.
transaction_contract: Cancellation is a multi-step write and MUST be atomic: the reversal-row insert, the balance release, the CANCEL audit record and the notification are one unit of work. Contract: every repository/service method that must join a caller's transaction takes an OPTIONAL trailing client?: PoolClient parameter and defaults to the shared pool when omitted (PgLeaveRequestRepository, PgLeaveBalanceRepository, PgAuditLogRepository, PgNotificationRepository, AuditService.record, NotificationService.create all already do this). The calling service owns the unit of work: LeaveService.cancel acquires a client via IUnitOfWork.withTransaction (PgUnitOfWork: pool.connect, BEGIN, run callback, COMMIT, ROLLBACK on throw, always release) and passes that client to repository.create (the reversal row), balanceRepository.findByKey(..., client, forUpdate = true), balanceRepository.update, auditService.record and notificationService.create. No repository ever opens BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. The DRAFT/SUBMITTED in-place path uses the same single transaction. Read paths (list, getById) open no transaction and forward no client.
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure -> HTTP 400 (ValidationError, code 'VALIDATION'); authentication failure -> HTTP 401 (UnauthorizedError, code 'UNAUTHORIZED'); authorization failure -> HTTP 403 (ForbiddenError, code 'FORBIDDEN'); not found -> HTTP 404 (NotFoundError, code 'NOT_FOUND'); invalid state transition or a second reversal of an already-reversed request -> HTTP 409 (ConflictError, code 'CONFLICT'); any other throw -> HTTP 500 with { error: 'Internal Server Error' }. `GET /leaves/:id` returns the same 404 for a request the caller may not see as for one that does not exist. `POST /leaves/:id/cancel` returns 200 with the resulting row: the mutated original for DRAFT/SUBMITTED, or the NEW CANCELLED reversal row (carrying reversesRequestId) for APPROVED.
